briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 launch intensifies frontier race as US export controls tighten on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated with new model releases from OpenAI and DeepSeek, while regulatory scrutiny on export controls and safety grows. Funding remains robust despite macro pressures, focused on compute and agentic systems. Prompt injection vulnerabilities continue to dominate production deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with enhanced multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus shows gains in long-context agent tasks. DeepSeek-V3 closed the gap on Western models with 1.2T parameter efficiency breakthroughs. Meta open-sourced Llama 4.1 while xAI scaled Grok-3 training.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and IoT deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp hits 1.2M units shipped. Microsoft expands Stargate data centers to 200k H100 equivalents. Google TPU v6 clusters now online in Iowa and Texas.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced AI chips slow China's frontier progress enough to maintain a 12-month US lead through 2027?
